newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big seller of Wal-Mart put.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big seller of Wal-Mart put.

text.p: A big seller of the Wal-Mart Stores September 35 put was seen Friday and was a feature as investors mainly wrapped up expiration-related activity, traders said.
The Wal-Mart September 35 put traded 17,600 contracts, making it the most active option around. The option, which had open interest of just 853 contracts, was down 1/8 at 7/8.
Wal-Mart shares eased 1/16 to 35-3/4 on more than four million shares amid a sharp broad market selloff.
"They sold them," Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said of the Wal-Mart September 35 calls.
By selling the puts, the investor or investors are basically willing to buy the stock at 35. If the stock falls below 35, the put buyer will have the right to sell the stock at that strike price.
Traders said much of the other activity in individual equity options was related to the expiration August contracts. The options go off the boards today and officially expire Saturday.
For instance, one trader noted that the Hewlett-Packard Co August 65 call traded about 10,850 contracts. The option had open interest of 15,039 going into today's session.
With the stock's 2-3/8-point drop, which put it at 67-1/2, the August 65 call lost 2-1/4 to 2-1/2.
The Hewlett-Packard September 65 call traded 7,545 contracts, a little more than double its open interest.
The trader said some of that volume could be from investors rolling August 65 call positions out to September. But some investors were likely selling those calls as well, he said.
One options trader said his desk had traded some Hewlett options, but most of his paper flow was two-way with no directional bias.
In other activity, K Mart Corp options continued active, particularly on the call side, as the stock struggled to hold its recent gains.
In late trade, K Mart was down 5/16 at 12-5/8 on consolidated volume of more than 3.7 million shares.
Trading again was led by the September 12-1/2 calls, which traded 3,550 contracts. The August 12-1/2 call traded 1,580.
The September 15, December 12-1/2 and 15 and January 15 calls also were busy. The most active K Mart put was the September 12-1/2 with turnover of about 450 contracts.
